summary: Todo is a small to-do list app where each person signs up, logs in and keeps their own list of tasks. It is built for anyone who wants a private checklist in the browser. An Express server stores users and todos in SQLite and issues JWT tokens, and a React client built with Vite calls its JSON API.

levels.name: Idea and scope
levels.goal: Decide what the app does: personal to-do lists behind a login. The README names the stack and what is out of scope (sharing, due dates, email reset).
levels.checkpoint: Explain the app in 3 sentences: who it is for, what it does, and how the server and client split the work.
levels.why_this_order: Commit #0 added the README and .gitignore before any code, so the idea came first.

levels.name: Project setup
levels.goal: Create the server package with its dependencies and the environment variables it needs (port, JWT secret, database file).
levels.checkpoint: npm install runs in server/ and the .env.example lists every variable the server reads.
levels.why_this_order: Commit #1 set up server/package.json and .env.example right after the idea.

levels.name: Data design
levels.goal: Design the users and todos tables, with each todo pointing at its owner through user_id.
levels.checkpoint: Draw the two tables and the user_id link between them.
levels.why_this_order: Commit #2 added schema.sql, and db.js reads it, so the schema has to exist first.

levels.name: Backend core
levels.goal: Open the SQLite database, build the Express app and add the todo routes for listing, adding, updating and deleting.
levels.checkpoint: GET /api/health returns { ok: true } and the todo routes read and write rows.
levels.why_this_order: Commits #2 and #3 added db.js, then the routes and app; routes/todos.js imports db.js and app.js imports the routes.

levels.name: Auth and sessions
levels.goal: Add signup and login with bcrypt password hashing, issue a JWT on login, and protect the todo routes with requireAuth.
levels.checkpoint: A request to /api/todos without a token gets 401 Not logged in.
levels.why_this_order: Commit #4 added the auth middleware and routes after the core routes existed to protect.

levels.name: Frontend skeleton
levels.goal: Create the Vite React client with its entry HTML, the App component and the Login and Todos screens.
levels.checkpoint: npm run dev in client/ shows the login form.
levels.why_this_order: Commit #5 added the whole React skeleton once the API was in place.

levels.name: Connect the two
levels.goal: Add one api.js module that calls the server with the stored token, and use it from the screens.
levels.checkpoint: After logging in, your real todos from the server show on screen.
levels.why_this_order: Commit #6 added api.js last, and both pages import it.

levels.name: Feature logic
levels.goal: The Todos screen: load, add, toggle and delete todos with a loading state.
levels.checkpoint: Use the app end to end: sign up, log in, add a todo, tick it and delete it.
levels.why_this_order: Todos.jsx imports api.js, so the feature logic comes after the connection layer.

levels.name: Validation and errors
levels.goal: The project has almost no input validation: titles are not checked and errors are not handled consistently.
levels.checkpoint: Sending an empty or 10,000-character todo title returns a clear 400 error instead of being stored.
levels.why_this_order: Validation hardens features that already work, so it comes after them.

levels.name: Testing
levels.goal: There are no tests in this project.
levels.checkpoint: A test suite covers signup, login and the todo routes, and passes.
levels.why_this_order: Tests lock in behaviour once the features exist.

levels.name: Security hardening
levels.goal: Fix the SQL injection in /search, the hard-coded JWT fallback secret, the open CORS policy and the HTML injection in the todo list.
levels.checkpoint: Your own audit finds no injection, no hard-coded secret and CORS limited to the client's origin.
levels.why_this_order: Hardening reviews code that already exists.

levels.name: Ship and maintain
levels.goal: There is no deployment, CI or logging setup.
levels.checkpoint: The app runs on a server with CI running tests on every push.
levels.why_this_order: Shipping comes last, once the app is tested and safe.
